item.title: Russia Continues to Improve the AK-12 Assault Rifle
item.description: The CEO of Russia’s famed Kalashnikov Concern announced that the company would redesign the AK-12 assault rifle in response to feedback from troops in Ukraine. The post Russia Continues to Improve the AK-12 Assault Rifle appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The B-21 Raider Could See Its First Deployment Next Year—and China Isn’t Happy
item.description: China can be content that the number of B-21 Raiders will likely remain fairly low—given its cost of nearly $700 million per aircraft. The post The B-21 Raider Could See Its First Deployment Next Year—and China Isn’t Happy appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The Muslim Brotherhood Is the Sudanese Regime
item.description: Sudan’s civil war won’t end, and civilian transition begin, until it faces its Muslim Brotherhood problem. The post The Muslim Brotherhood Is the Sudanese Regime appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: An American Aircraft Carrier Is Still on the Way to Iran
item.description: Though President Trump has been widely criticized for promising a strike on Iran and failing to deliver, it may only be a matter of time. The post An American Aircraft Carrier Is Still on the Way to Iran appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: How Great Power Politics Is Undermining Europe’s Green Transition
item.description: The removal of Nicolas Maduro marks the arrival of a Trumpian geopolitical era defined by blunt realism. Advocates of the green transition would do best to realize that. item.title: The USS Roosevelt (DDG-80) and Donald Trump’s March on Iran
item.description: Trump’s naval buildup around Iran mirrors his buildup near Venezuela—raising the possibility that a similar strike on Iran’s leadership might follow. The post The USS Roosevelt (DDG-80) and Donald Trump’s March on Iran appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: This Royal Navy Submarine Is Traveling to the Land Down Under
item.description: The HMS Anson is the fifth Astute-class fast attack submarine in Royal Navy service—and the eighth vessel to bear the name of George Anson, an 18th-century British admiral. The post This Royal Navy Submarine Is Traveling to the Land Down Under appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Why Denmark Just Retired Its Last American-Made F-16 Fighter Jets
item.description: Although tensions are running high between Denmark and the United States over the status of Greenland, the retirement of the F-16s is unrelated to the current crisis. item.title: Why Did the US Navy Just Send a Strike Force into the Indo-Pacific?
item.description: Beyond a vague commitment to “maintaining peace and security,” it is not yet clear what the Tripoli Expeditionary Strike Group’s aims in the Indo-Pacific are. The post Why Did the US Navy Just Send a Strike Force into the Indo-Pacific? appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: America’s Indo-Pacific Forces Are Getting a Hypersonic Missile Upgrade
item.description: At the end of 2025, the US Army announced that its “Bravo Battery” would host batteries of the Dark Eagle hypersonic missile—replacing the M142 HIMARS it currently operates.
